clinical_note: Aorta gives rise to Left Main and Left Anterior Descending coronary artery.
LAD septal perforators supply anterior 2/3 of interventricular septum.
LAD wraps around the cardiac apex, providing critical apical perfusion.
LAD diagonal branches supply the anterior left ventricular free wall.
Right Coronary Artery supplies the right atrium and SA nodal artery.
RCA acute marginal branches supply the right ventricular anterior/inferior wall.
Left Circumflex supplies the lateral left atrium.
LCX obtuse marginal branches supply the lateral and posterior left ventricle.
Superior Vena Cava returns upper systemic venous blood into Right Atrium.
Inferior Vena Cava returns lower systemic venous blood into Right Atrium.
Blood passes through the Tricuspid Valve during ventricular diastole.
Tricuspid valve directs deoxygenated flow into Right Ventricle.
Right ventricle contracts in systole, opening the Pulmonary Valve.
Pulmonary valve ejects blood into the Pulmonary Trunk.
Right pulmonary artery conducts flow to Right Lung microcirculation.
Left pulmonary artery conducts flow to Left Lung microcirculation.
Right pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to Left Atrium.
Left pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to Left Atrium.
Oxygenated blood passes across the Mitral Valve during left ventricular filling.
Mitral valve fills the Left Ventricle.
Left ventricular high-pressure systolic contraction forces open the Aortic Valve.
Aortic valve ejects blood into the Ascending Aorta.
Ascending aorta distributes cardiac output into the Aortic Arch.
Sternum directly occludes anterior line of sight to heart.
Ribcage and costal cartilages enclose and occlude thoracic viscera.
Ribcage encloses right lung.
Ribcage encloses left lung.
Right atrium is a component chamber of the heart.
Right ventricle is a component chamber of the heart.
Left atrium is a component chamber of the heart.
Left ventricle is a component chamber of the heart.
Interventricular septum divides the cardiac ventricles.
Cardiac apex is part of the left ventricle.
